nodes.title: 1. MODELS + GPU
widgets_values:
## Models, folders and your GPU

**Each loader reads a DIFFERENT folder.** A model in the wrong folder simply
will not appear in the dropdown (the widget shows red).

| loader | folder |
|---|---|
| Diffusion model | `models/diffusion_models/` |
| Video VAE | `models/vae/` |
| Text projection + Audio VAE | `models/checkpoints/` |
| Gemma text encoder | `models/text_encoders/` |

**Which build for which card** (set on the Diffusion model node; `weight_dtype`
there can also drop it to fp8 without a separate file):

| your GPU | use |
|---|---|
| 32 GB+ (5090) | bf16, `weight_dtype = default` |
| 24 GB (3090/4090) | bf16 with `weight_dtype = fp8_e4m3fn`, or a Q8_0 GGUF |
| 16 GB | Q5_0 / Q4_0 GGUF |

**System RAM matters more than VRAM here.** Loading copies the whole checkpoint
into system RAM. On 64 GB set a Windows pagefile of 64-128 GB on an SSD, or
ComfyUI can be killed by the OS mid-load with no Python error.

nodes.title: 0. GLOBAL
widgets_values:
## Global settings - one place, every shot

`width` / `height` / `length` here feed BOTH shots, so shots always match -
they must, or the chain breaks (shot 2 starts on shot 1's last frame, and the
model cannot bridge a resolution change).

* width and height: divisible by 32. Landscape 960x544 or 768x512;
  portrait 544x960 or 512x768.
* `length` must be 8n+1: 97, 241, 497, 1001... duration = length / 25.

**Three things still set per shot (they cannot be derived in-graph):**
1. `LTXV Empty Latent Audio` -> `frames_number` = length (modes 1-2 only,
   capped at 1000 - irrelevant in mode 3, where that node never runs)
2. `LAST FRAME` (ImageFromBatch in THE CHAIN) -> `batch_index` = length - 1
3. Trim durations: shot 1 covers `start .. start + length/25`; the shot-2 trim
   starts where shot 1 ends. The FINISH group joins them in order.

nodes.title: PROMPT RULES
widgets_values:
## Writing the prompt

**Only the text inside "double quotes" should be spoken.** But the model has a
narrator prior: left to itself it will happily read your scene description out
loud too. It is not enough to put the line in quotes - you have to say what it
must NOT do.

These prompts therefore carry an explicit exclusivity block:

> They are the only person speaking, and the only voice on the audio track is
> theirs. One continuous line with natural breaths and brief pauses. **No
> narration, no voice-over, no other speech, and nothing else is read aloud.**

Keep that block when you rewrite the prompt. Dropping it is what makes the
model recite your whole paragraph.

**Other rules that carry over from the full pack:**
* ~26-32 spoken words per shot. Much longer and delivery drifts.
* ONE speaker per shot. Two quoted lines in one prompt tend to come out
  simultaneously, in the same voice.
* Say the accent explicitly if it matters ("a casual American accent") - it
  drifts otherwise, often to British.
* Describe what should HAPPEN, not a fixed person or place, if you are using a
  reference image - a prompt that contradicts the image makes the model fight
  the guide.
* In **mode 3** delete the quoted line entirely; your audio file supplies the
  words and a quote competes with it.

The person in frame stands still, facing the camera, and speaks. They are the only person speaking, and the only voice on the audio track is theirs. One continuous line with natural breaths and brief pauses. No narration, no voice-over, no other speech, and nothing else is read aloud. Their first mouth movement begins with the first audible word and the mouth settles after the final word. At a calm, even speed, the lip movement aligning closely with the audio throughout the line, they say, "I have been waiting here since this morning." The camera does not move.
nodes.title: Shot 1 prompt
2. LENGTH + RESOLUTION
widgets_values:
## Length and resolution

**Duration = `length` / `fps`.** Right now 241 / 25 = **9.6 seconds** per shot.

`length` MUST be **8n+1**: 97, 145, 241, 329, 417, 497...
(97 = ~3.9s, 241 = ~9.6s, 497 = ~19.9s at 25 fps)

**If you change `length`, change these too or the shot breaks:**
1. `LTXV Empty Latent Audio` -> `frames_number` = the same number
2. `ImageFromBatch` (in THE CHAIN group) -> `batch_index` = length - 1

**Resolution** must be divisible by 32 on both axes. Safe combos:
`768x512` (fast tests) - `1024x576` - `1280x704` - `1344x768` (16:9 quality)
Portrait: `576x1024`, `768x1344`.

Bigger costs VRAM *and* time roughly with width x height x length. Test at
768x512 / 97 frames first, then scale up once the shot is right.

**fps 25** is what this model family is rendered at. The Lightricks MSR sample
uses 50; at 50 the same frames play in half the time and motion looks fast.

nodes.title: 3. AUDIO MODES
widgets_values:
## Audio - two modes

**Mode 1 (default) - the character speaks in YOUR reference voice.**
This is how the workflow ships. Point `LoadAudio` at a clean speech sample
and the model speaks your prompt's quoted line in that voice.

* `LoadAudio` (node `5.`) = 3-5 seconds of clean, solo, continuous speech.
  No music, no second speaker, no long silences.
* `5b. Trim` controls how much is used: `start_index` = where to start
  (seconds), `duration` = how much. **Length matters** - the WHOLE clip
  becomes conditioning tokens, so a long sample hands the model extra words
  to echo ("my line plus garbled extra words"). Keep it short.
* Requires the **ID-LoRA** (node `1b.` in SETUP). Reference-audio identity
  transfer is a trained adapter, not a base-model skill - without it the
  model echoes fragments of your clip instead of adopting the voice.

**Mode 2 - let the model invent a voice.**
* BYPASS the reference node - there is ONE PER SHOT, so box-select both and
  press Ctrl+B once (they turn purple).
* Everything else is unchanged. The prompt's quoted line is still spoken.

The audio you hear is always what the model generated - there is no track
substitution.

**If audio garbles in Mode 1:** shorten the trim toward 3s, and lower
`identity_guidance_scale` toward 1.5 where that widget exists. Note
`identity_guidance_scale = 0` is NOT a clean control - it only skips the
guidance pass, the reference tokens stay attached. Only Ctrl+B removes them.

**LIP-SYNC POLISH:** the bypassed LatentSync node in the FINISH group
re-animates mouths to match the audio - a dedicated lip-sync model, tighter
than native generation. Ctrl+B to enable; costs a second diffusion pass.

nodes.title: 4. THE CHAIN
widgets_values:
## How the chain works

`ImageFromBatch` pulls the **last frame** of shot 1 and hands it to shot 2's
`LTXVAddGuide` at `frame_idx 0`. That is the whole trick: shot 2 starts on the
exact frame shot 1 ended on, so the two cut together.

`batch_index` must be **length - 1**. If you change `length`, change this too.

**To add shot 3:** copy the SHOT 2 group, add another `ImageFromBatch` fed from
shot 2's `VAEDecode`, and wire it into the new shot's `LTXVAddGuide.image`.

**What this is not:** there is no memory bank here. Continuity comes only from
the handed-over frame, so identity drifts over many shots. That is the honest
ceiling of the "lite" approach - the JoyAI-Echo node pack exists because a
paired audio+video memory bank cannot run on a stock sampler.

The same person, in the same place, still facing the camera, speaks again. They are the only person speaking, and the only voice on the audio track is theirs. One continuous line with natural breaths and brief pauses. No narration, no voice-over, no other speech, and nothing else is read aloud. Their first mouth movement begins with the first audible word and the mouth settles after the final word. At a calm, even speed, the lip movement aligning closely with the audio throughout the line, they say, "I am not waiting any longer." The camera does not move.
nodes.title: Shot 2 prompt
5. FINISH
widgets_values:
## The final file

Shots 1 and 2 are joined here (video and audio, in order) and refined with a
deterministic 1.5x upscale: bicubic + a gentle sharpen. Deterministic on
purpose - generative refiners re-invent detail per frame, which reads as
texture shimmer; bicubic + sharpen beat every generative option in a side-by-
side tournament on this model's output. Turn refine off by setting `scale_by`
to 1.0 and `alpha` to 0.

The per-shot SaveVideo files are previews; **publish this one**
(`multishot_lite/FINAL`).

Note: shot 2's first frame IS shot 1's last frame (that is the chain), so the
joint holds one duplicated frame - 1/25th of a second, invisible at a hard cut.

**LIP-SYNC POLISH (PLUS only):** the bypassed LatentSync node between the join
and the upscale re-animates the mouth to match the audio track exactly - a
dedicated lip-sync model, much tighter than native generation for external
audio. Select it and Ctrl+B to enable. Costs a second diffusion pass (roughly
real-time x2-4). `lips_expression` = mouth movement intensity (1.5 default;
raise toward 2.5 for rap). Works best on near-frontal faces at 25 fps - which
is what this graph produces.

**The sharpen node ships BYPASSED, on purpose.** Core `ImageSharpen` moves the
entire batch to the GPU and allocates two more full-size copies (pad + conv), so
it needs about 3x the batch in VRAM. A few hundred frames is fine - Ctrl+B to
enable it. A 2000-frame run OOMs a 32 GB card at any resolution. The upscale
itself has no such limit (it runs on CPU).

For long runs, sharpen the finished file instead - this is the same
contrast-adaptive recipe, and it takes seconds:

```
ffmpeg -i FINAL.mp4 -vf "cas=0.55" -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -preset medium        -tune grain -bf 0 -c:a copy FINAL_sharp.mp4
```

Long runs: the join + upscale holds all frames in system RAM as floats. Two
1001-frame shots at 960x544 upscaled 1.5x is roughly 20 GB of RAM - fine on
64 GB+, but set scale_by to 1.0 if RAM is tight.

groups.title: SETUP - models and inputs (set these, then queue)
GLOBAL - set resolution and length ONCE for all shots
SHOT 1  -  PROMPT (what happens + the spoken line)
THE CHAIN - shot 1's last frame becomes shot 2's first
SHOT 2  -  PROMPT (what happens + the spoken line)
FINISH - both shots joined + deterministic 1.5x refine
